quotations.quote: That consent is not required for a reorganization within a wholly owned group if Provider remains responsible for its obligations under this Agreement.

analysis: The modified Section 12.6 in the Key Terms replaces the Standard Terms version and controls per the Framework Terms hierarchy. The provision addresses two distinct triggers: (1) assignment of rights or obligations requires consent; (2) change of control of Provider requires consent. A third sentence provides an exception to the change-of-control consent requirement only. A 'proposed internal reorganisation' does not by itself establish either trigger. An internal reorganisation could involve an assignment, a change of control, both, or neither. Without knowing what transaction Equator proposes, we cannot determine whether any consent requirement is engaged. If a trigger is established, the exception to change-of-control consent requires two cumulative conditions (wholly owned group AND continued responsibility), neither of which is evidenced.
conclusion: Whether Victoria's consent is required is unresolved. Neither an assignment nor a change of control is established on current evidence; a proposed internal reorganisation alone triggers neither. Victoria should ask Equator to confirm: (1) whether the Agreement will be assigned to another entity; (2) whether a change of control of Equator will occur; (3) if either applies, the ownership chart demonstrating wholly owned group status; and (4) written confirmation that Equator remains responsible for all obligations.
